Troubleshooting · BEGINNER FRIENDLY · 7 MIN READ

Why is my computer running slowly?

Tech Compass · Updated 2026-10-19

IN THIS GUIDE

The quick answer1. Restart, then observe2. Look for the bottleneck3. Make room and reduce startup work4. Check updates and airflowWhen to consider an upgradeFurther reading
THE QUICK ANSWER

A slow computer may be short of memory or storage space, busy with background work, or getting too hot. Start by finding what is busy instead of installing a cleaner app.

1. Restart, then observe

Save your work and restart. Open only the app you need. Note whether the slowdown starts immediately, after opening a particular app, or after the computer has been running for a while.

2. Look for the bottleneck

In Windows Task Manager or macOS Activity Monitor, inspect CPU and memory usage. A high number during a demanding task is normal. A program that stays busy when you are doing nothing deserves a closer look. Do not end unfamiliar system processes.

3. Make room and reduce startup work

Review your Downloads folder and uninstall apps you no longer use through system settings. Back up files before removing them. Review startup or login items and disable optional apps you recognize. Do not delete system folders.

4. Check updates and airflow

Install supported operating-system and app updates. Keep ventilation openings clear and use a laptop on a hard surface. If the device is unusually hot, shuts itself down, or has a swollen battery, stop using it and seek qualified service.

When to consider an upgrade

Measure first. Consistently high memory pressure may justify more RAM if the device supports it. A storage bottleneck may improve with an SSD. Check compatibility and back up your data before hardware work.

Explanation · 4 MIN READ

What is RAM?

RAM is your computer’s short-term working memory. It holds the information your apps are using right now. Storage keeps your files when the power is off; RAM does not.

Read the guide ↗Explanation · 4 MIN READ

SSD vs. HDD: what’s the difference?

An SSD stores data in flash memory. An HDD stores it on spinning magnetic platters. Both keep files without power, but SSDs usually access data much faster.

What to do when a computer won’t start

Separate a power problem from a display or startup problem. Check for indicator lights, fan noise, and anything on the screen before deciding what to try.
